result:
I ran the plan with executing-dag-plans: all 16 tasks are done, none failed or were skipped, and every test suite passes when I run them myself.

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| plan-state | 257 passed, 0 failed |
| verify-tests | 48 passed, 0 failed |
| resolve-declared-paths | 91 passed, 0 failed |
| audit-stats | 8 passed, 0 failed |
| commit-safe (concurrent-commit, stale-lock) | PASS, PASS |

Each suite exited 0, and `git worktree list` shows the same 7 entries as before the run, so no test worktrees were left behind.

**What was built** (18 commits on `d2/run-962d94`, from `7327891` to `2fa119f`):
- **`plan-state`:** reads the new `tests:` field and checks it (rule 16). When a task is set running it records the commit it started from in `base_sha:` (rule 17). A new `plan-state tests` command prints a task's named tests.
- **`skills/executing-dag-plans/verify-tests`:** a new script. It builds a before tree and an after tree in throwaway worktrees and labels each named test `ok`, `ok-absent`, `not-red`, `not-green` or `ambiguous`. For failures it prints the last lines of the test output. It cleans up on every exit path, including Ctrl-C and kill signals.
- **Docs and prompts:** the executor now marks a task running before dispatch and runs `verify-tests` before review, and a failed check counts as a fix round. The implementer and reviewer prompts, the plan format, new rule S17, the planner, the updater, the plan audit, the README and `CLAUDE.md` all describe named tests.

**Review notes:**
- task-base-sha needed one fix round: a required test name was split into two cases.
- Two reviewers left out the closing verdict line, so I re-ran each once; both re-runs approved.
- Before review, I sent task-format back to fix wording that didn't match the spec. That didn't count as a fix round.

**Things to look at:**
- **Two commits have no Co-Authored-By trailer:** `aad4d2f` (tests field) and `00e05fb` (base_sha). Later commits sit on top of them. One implementer tried `git commit --amend` and the permission check refused it, so I didn't do it myself. If you want the trailers, it means rewriting the branch history.
- **One acceptance criterion predicted the wrong label.** The plan expected the case `round on "2" counts to 3` to come out `ok`; it came out `not-red`. Commit `76ed77d` shows that case already passed before the fix it was meant to prove, so the label is right. The sibling case `round on "2" writes review_rounds: 3` comes out `ok`. Both results are recorded in the `verify-tests` header.
- **Bash tool timeouts send no signal.** On a timeout the tool moved the command to the background and let it finish, instead of stopping it. A test run can therefore outlast the 600000 ms the executor text assumes. A kill signal can't be cleaned up after: the leftover worktrees are cleared only once the temp directory is gone. The executor text may need an `/update` to say this.
- **Two portability gaps:** I couldn't test `verify-tests` under mawk or busybox awk because neither is installed here; it passed under gawk and `gawk --posix`. If its suite is started with a shell `&`, the Ctrl-C test case fails, because the children then ignore Ctrl-C.
- **Speed:** running `verify-tests` against this repo's plan-state suite takes about 5–6 minutes, because it runs the suite twice.

The plan file's status changes are uncommitted (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-17-named-tests.md`); I can commit them if you want. The per-task body files I extracted for the subagents are in `C:/Users/Brett/d2-runs/pde-962d94-work/`, outside the repo, and can be deleted.
